findings.title: KeyError crash when Integration metadata lacks sender
findings.body: In src/sentry/integrations/github/integration.py line 503 GitHubInstallation does integration.metadata["sender"]["login"] with direct indexing. Integrations created before this feature, created via the fresh-install path in build_integration which only sets sender if state has it, or with webhook payloads lacking sender will have no "sender" key. Direct indexing raises KeyError resulting in a 500 instead of the intended install-failed page, blocking legitimate second-org installs and reinstalls after upgrade.

findings.title: Unhandled token exchange/user lookup errors cause 500
findings.body: In src/sentry/integrations/github/integration.py OAuthLoginView calls safe_urlopen to exchange code for access_token and get_user_info to fetch login outside any handling; only body parsing is in try/except. Network errors, timeouts, non-2xx from GitHub, or ApiError from /user propagate as 500. The PR description says bad/reused code and failed token generation should show the install-failed page, but those paths crash instead of returning error().

findings.title: First-time installs skip GitHub-user verification
findings.body: In src/sentry/integrations/github/integration.py GitHubInstallation only compares github_authenticated_user to sender when an Integration row already exists. On Integration.DoesNotExist it immediately returns pipeline.next_step() and build_integration creates the Integration without ever checking the authenticated user. An attacker who guesses an unused sequential installation_id or wins the webhook race can link a victim GitHub installation to their own Sentry org, defeating the hijack protection that only covers the already-exists branch.

findings.title: Pipeline state mutated before OAuth state validation
findings.body: In src/sentry/integrations/github/integration.py OAuthLoginView binds request installation_id into persistent pipeline state before checking if request state equals pipeline.signature. A request with an invalid state still poisons the stored installation_id. The later legitimate GitHub callback with valid state and no installation_id then reuses the poisoned value via fetch_state fallback in GitHubInstallation, enabling installation_id fixation across steps. State must be validated before any bind_state.

findings.title: Installation-not-found and token-failure paths no longer tested
findings.body: In tests/sentry/integrations/github/test_integration.py test_installation_not_found stubs 404 for /app/installations but then drives setup with state ddd023... which does not match the pipeline signature, so OAuthLoginView rejects on state mismatch before build_integration ever calls GitHub. The test never exercises the 404 handling it names, and there are no tests for missing access_token, code reuse, or explicit state mismatch, leaving the new security-critical branches without coverage.
